explanation:
[EFFECT] Each day of the week shows a wide spread of SHAP values, reflecting how the model interacts the day with other conditions (particularly hour). Sunday (0) and Saturday (6) span the widest range (roughly −0.9 to +0.6 and −0.65 to +0.55 respectively), while mid-week days cluster somewhat more narrowly around or slightly above zero. There is no simple monotonic trend across the seven days.
[IMPORTANCE] The total vertical range is roughly 1.4–1.5 log-units, making weekday one of the higher-importance features after hour, though much of its spread reflects strong interactions with time of day.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
